::: {.audience-section}
[A Note for Specific Audiences]{.section-label}

::: {.audience}
### Prospective PhD Students

::: {.audience-body}
I take students through [Terry's MIS doctoral program](https://www.terry.uga.edu/phd/management-information-systems/). Strong candidates typically have quantitative training (statistics, computer science, engineering, or a quantitative social science), some research exposure, and a substantive interest in one or more of my research streams.

The best way to gauge fit is to read a recent paper of mine and tell me what you'd do differently. Generic interest emails are fine, but specific ones get specific answers.
:::
:::

::: {.audience}
### Workshops & Consulting Inquiries

::: {.audience-body}
Briefly describe your organization, audience, and what you're hoping to accomplish. Most engagements start with a 30-minute call to scope. See [workshops & consulting](workshops.qmd) for current offerings.
:::
:::

::: {.audience}
### Media & Speaking

::: {.audience-body}
Happy to talk to journalists about human-AI collaboration, algorithmic decision-making, computational social science, or open-source software dynamics.
:::
:::

::: {.audience}
### Research Collaboration

::: {.audience-body}
I'm always interested in conversations with researchers working on adjacent problems — relational and sequential data methods, human-AI teaming, large-group coordination, or the methodology of measuring AI's effects on work. Email with a sentence or two on what you're working on.
:::
:::
:::
